=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/assemble_agents.py | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The review raised a concern that parse_fragment might treat agents section markers inside fenced code blocks as sections.
  WHY: The reviewer states the fence check runs before section parsing and that the concern was a misunderstanding of the existing logic, not a runtime failure.
- scripts/build_static_context.sh | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: If `assemble_agents.py render` fails, `_static_context_cat_agents` silently falls back to `cat "${agents_file}"`.
  WHY: This can hide fragment assembly errors and give the orchestrator model static context that omits fragments, contrary to the documented contract.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate.yml | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The workflow warns that agents.md is omitted when it is a broken symlink, even if AGENTS.md exists and is subsequently used.
  WHY: The warning then falsely claims the agents section is omitted from static context.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- requirement: "the AGENTS.md materiality check and the review gate count an agents.d/*.md change as an agents.md change"
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_agents_md_materiality.sh and .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml

- requirement: Readers render pending fragments into the model’s agents context, including when a valid `new` fragment is the only agents documentation.
  expected_change_site: scripts/build_static_context.sh::_static_context_local_agents_file / emit_agents_md and .github/workflows/orchestrate.yml “Pre-assemble static context”
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `_static_context_local_agents_file` returns an empty string and `emit_agents_md` skips rendering when neither agents.md nor AGENTS.md exists; the orchestrate.yml reader renders only when `orchestrate_agents_file` is non-empty, so a valid `new` fragment alone is absent from model context until assembly.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

Even though `review_autofix.yml` was updated, the helper script itself remains restricted to the exact filename "agents.md".
  severity=high

  severity=high

  Requirement: The PR description says the shared reader should ensure “nothing is missed in between” and that pending fragments are rendered into the model’s agents context.
  Expected change site: `scripts/build_static_context.sh` and the matching agents-file selection in `.github/workflows/orchestrate.yml` / `orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml` / `validate_process.sh`.
  Evidence of absence: In environments where no `agents.md` or `AGENTS.md` file exists (but an `agents.d/` fragment does), the static context assembler (`_static_context_local_agents_file`) returns an empty string, and `emit_agents_md` skips rendering entirely, thus failing to show the pending fragment to the model.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/orchestrate.yml | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: When `agents.md` is a broken symlink (so `[ -f agents.md ]` is false and `[ -L agents.md ]` is true) but `AGENTS.md` exists as a regular file, the first `elif` emits `::warning::agents.md is a symbolic link; omitted from the static context.` before the second branch falls back to `AGENTS.md` and emits the agents section.
  WHY: A consumer repo that sets up `agents.md` as a dangling or symbolic pointer but keeps `AGENTS.md` as the real file will see a misleading GitHub Actions warning on every orchestrator run, and an operator who follows the warning text will look for the missing agents section that is in fact being emitted.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "the AGENTS.md materiality check and the review gate count an agents.d/*.md change as an agents.md change" (PR description, "AGENTS.md materiality check and the review gate"), supported by CLAUDE.md §30 which explicitly recognises both `agents.md` and `AGENTS.md` casings as first-class. The scope guard (`scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:307-316`) and reject verifier (`scripts/review_reject_verify.sh:359-365`) already handle both casings.
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_agents_md_materiality.sh:356-359` and `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1536-1540` (`result["agents_md_changed"] = "agents.md" in changed_paths` / `"agents.md" in seen`).
  Evidence of absence: Both sites only check for the lowercase path. A consumer repo that updates its `AGENTS.md` directly (or via a fragment targeting an existing `AGENTS.md`) keeps `"AGENTS.md"` (uppercase) in its changed-path set; `"agents.md" in changed_paths` is False, `agents_md_changed=False`, and the consolidator's Lens 7 emits the "agents.md unchanged" finding even though the file was updated. The contract the rest of §30 implements treats `AGENTS.md` as equivalent to `agents.md`, so the materiality check is the only site that does not.
  severity=high
  confidence=[3]
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: PR description — "Following Q43 A, fragments are folded at release time, like `changelog.d/`, with a shared reader so nothing is missed in between." `scripts/assemble_agents.py::apply_block` already supports a `<!-- agents: section="<new heading>" new -->` block that creates a section in a brand-new agents file (the existing `test_consumer_casing_and_missing_file` test exercises this: an empty repo plus a `new` fragment produces `AGENTS.md` from scratch).
  Expected change site: `scripts/build_static_context.sh::emit_agents_md` (and `_static_context_local_agents_file` if the helper gains a "synthesise from fragments" branch), and the corresponding `orchestrate_agents_file` block in `.github/workflows/orchestrate.yml`.
  Evidence of absence: Both readers gate the fragment-render branch on a pre-existing `agents.md` or `AGENTS.md` (`emit_agents_md` only renders when `_static_context_local_agents_file` succeeded; `orchestrate.yml` only renders when `orchestrate_agents_file` is non-empty). A repo whose first agents.md contribution is a `new` fragment will see no agents context at all until the release fold, which is exactly the "missed in between" the description rules out.
  severity=high
  confidence=[4]
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
